about: How an Agent record's `scope:` and `read-scope:` read, and which paths a scope admits (M58.6). `parse`: a key filed under relationships (a [[link]], CV-09) names no folder, so it is []; an absent key is null, which is unrestricted; a present key that is null, a number, a boolean or a mapping is [] (fail closed: a missing field must never widen access); a string is one folder and an array keeps its strings; each folder is trimmed, loses every leading ./ and its leading and trailing /, and an empty one is dropped. `admits`: null admits every path and [] none; a folder admits itself and its descendants, matched at a separator, after the path loses every leading ./ and then its leading /, and the folder its outer /; an empty folder admits every path; case and Unicode form compare exactly, and .. compares as written, since the note door refuses it before any scope is asked. Replayed by replays_the_shared_scope_cases and a_handed_off_run_reads_its_folders_as_the_page_does in src-tauri/src/mcp.rs, a_thread_turn_reads_its_folders_as_the_page_does in src-tauri/src/agent/thread_turn.rs, and src/engine/agentAccess.test.ts. `name` is for the reader.

parse.name: a bare key scopes to nothing
a list keeps its folders in order
spelling around a folder is not part of it
a folder that trims to nothing is dropped
the vault folder spelled . is kept as written
a list keeps only its strings
a list with no string scopes to nothing
an empty list scopes to nothing
a [[link]] is a relation, not a folder
the read axis reads the same grammar
an absent read scope reads everywhere
an empty read scope reads nowhere
a bare read scope reads nowhere
one axis never reads the other's key

admits.name: no scope admits every path
an empty scope admits nothing
a folder admits itself, which create_note targets
a folder admits what sits in it
and what sits deeper
a longer folder name is another folder
a file named like the folder is not in it
a sibling sharing a prefix is not in it
a path spelled with ./ is the same path
a path spelled with a leading / is the same path
a folder written with a trailing /
a folder written with a leading /
case compares exactly
Unicode form compares exactly
a nested folder admits its own pages
a nested folder's prefix sibling is outside
a nested folder's parent is outside
two folders admit either
two folders admit nothing else
the vault root is outside a folder
the vault root is inside no scope
an empty folder admits every path, though no parser emits one
.. compares as written; the note door refuses it first
